claims.statement: The shared chat-command registry supplies host parsing, `/help`, and platform advertisements where supported; `/reset-all-history` and `/pair` are hidden but remain executable, while `/model` is visible.

The CLI attaches WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, and Slack adapters from explicit flags or corresponding enabled environment variables; with no model it uses the echo runtime, while a model opens configured checkpoint and history stores, loads MCP tools, and builds the Deep Agents runtime.
Channel exposure is shared as `self`, `allowlist`, or explicitly acknowledged `open`; open exposure permits arbitrary senders to trigger the agent with operator credentials and local-host access.
Discord registers visible shared commands as native slash commands when enabled, whereas Slack exposes one app-owned slash command and requires bot mention plus typed command text in channel threads.

`/model` selection is assistant-wide: an operator can choose a credentialed provider-catalog model or the default, and the saved choice applies on the next turn across chats and persists across `/new` and restarts; scheduled jobs and subagents retain their configured or startup models.

Talon loads MCP tools from the configured provider at runtime startup and exposes CLI configuration-path and OAuth-login commands; manual MCP configuration changes can be reloaded through `/mcp-reload`.

Without a sandbox, agent shell and file tools run on the host; with a model configured, a requested sandbox is opened for the model-host lifetime and startup fails rather than falling back to host execution. An attached sandbox is retained, while Talon closes an owned sandbox on exit and after a cancelled startup handoff.

Talon is experimental and does not provide production-grade complete HITL policy, channel administrator controls, or multi-tenant boundaries; its sandbox does not cover MCP tools, and admitted channel access should be treated as access to the operator's credentials and host resources.

Sender pairing is limited to Discord, Slack, and Telegram; operator approval consumes a channel-bound short-lived code, pairing grants admission rather than operator authority, and unreadable persisted pairing state fails closed.

MCP reload builds replacement runtime tools and graph under a lock; a refresh failure leaves the previous graph usable and marks the MCP reload inactive, while active tasks keep their original capabilities.

Talon converts readable inbound images of at most 5 MiB into bounded multimodal base64 image blocks and inlines allowlisted text documents only through 100 KiB; outbound Markdown media must resolve to a supported image or video regular file beneath the trusted outbound root and rejects URLs, traversal, absolute or home paths, and symlink escapes.

LangSmith tracing runs only when `LANGSMITH_TRACING` is truthy and `LANGSMITH_API_KEY` is present; each traced invocation is tagged and annotated with Talon assistant, conversation, trigger, and request metadata, while a missing optional package degrades to a warning without tracing.
The optional local activity logger records agent, model-lifecycle, and tool events; tool input/output previews are redacted, structurally bounded, and truncated to 1,000 characters.

Slack uses Socket Mode, acknowledges envelopes before handling them, deduplicates recent event IDs, and treats a DM as one conversation while mapping each mentioned channel thread to its own conversation.

The host starts the agent runtime before adapters and the scheduler, unwinds already-started components after startup failure, and on shutdown cancels work before stopping channels, scheduler, and runtime.
A scheduler is attached only when at least one channel exists, and a scheduled result is delivered only through the channel serving its recorded origin; otherwise it is dropped.
Pairing state uses locked atomic updates, and the CLI warns that `pairing pause-jobs` must run while Talon is stopped because the live host is the cron store's only writer.

A new message in an active conversation cancels the existing turn, records an interruption marker after the latest committed checkpoint, and starts the new message on the same thread; a cancellation that exceeds 30 seconds blocks the new turn and requires a host restart for recovery.

ConversationSaver archives channel conversations so they survive restarts and context compaction; `/new` retains earlier sessions, while `/reset-all-history` deletes only the current chat's archive sessions and checkpoints and does not delete cron jobs, memory, media, traces, or backups.
Talon 0.0.9 requires Python 3.12 or later and provides the `deepagents-talon` CLI entry point.

`DEEPAGENTS_TALON_CHECKPOINT_URI` selects local SQLite, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, or an operator-installed checkpoint backend; built-in schemes take precedence, and unknown or duplicate plugin schemes fail configuration.

Checkpoint and history storage are independently configurable; remote checkpoint thread IDs are not automatically assistant-namespaced, so operators should use separate databases for separate assistants.
The checkpoint factory opens the selected saver for the model host and `ConversationSaver` wraps it with the independently opened history archive before constructing the runtime.

Each Talon assistant has a validated, namespaced home under `~/.deepagents/<assistant-id>` by default, with restrictive home, manifest, agents, cron, channel, and inbound-media directories; it also installs defaults and ensures the assistant tool-approval store exists.

The history archive can use SQLite, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, or exactly one trusted installed history-backend plugin for a URI scheme; it namespaces archive data by assistant ID and initializes the archive before the model host begins.

Sandbox mode routes execution and ordinary filesystem operations to the sandbox, while only assistant `skills/`, `memory/`, and `/blobs/` are host routes; host blobs persist in assistant artifacts across recreated sandboxes and other assistant state, MCP tools, web tools, and channel media handling remain outside this sandbox boundary.

The host binds each adapter's inbound callback, derives a provider-qualified conversation root, serializes processing by that root, and dispatches commands or replaces the active agent turn before delivering the result back through the adapter.

Optional semantic history search is enabled with `DEEPAGENTS_TALON_HISTORY_VECTOR_SEARCH`; a changed embedding profile requires explicit `DEEPAGENTS_TALON_HISTORY_REINDEX=1` to rebuild the vector index while retaining transcripts.

Slack channel threads have separate active conversations and reply destinations but share archive history at channel scope; bounded preceding replies from operators and allowlisted users are added as thread context by default, while an explicit setting can include other participants.

A scheduled run holds a per-job conversation lock, has a 30-minute bound, and repairs its interrupted runtime thread after timeout; when channel history is available, it reads the recorded origin chat's history scope.

Slack translates an app-owned slash command of any manifest name into a shared typed Talon command, accepts it only in a DM except for operator pairing approval, and uses the validated Slack response URL for private command results and rejections.
Slack excludes loopback OAuth callback URLs from retrieved thread context before truncation, preventing callback secrets from being injected into a later model request.

Slack file handling sends the bot token only to HTTPS files.slack.com downloads and rejects redirects; capped downloads use no-follow, owner-only local-file creation and remove partial files after failure.

The default host backend uses a local shell rooted at `DEEPAGENTS_TALON_WORKSPACE` when set, passes a scrubbed allowlist of environment values with a fixed safe `PATH`, and stores binary artifacts under the assistant home.
The host passes inbound image blocks in request metadata, and filesystem middleware offloads the binary once so checkpoint messages do not retain the base64 image while the model request can use it.
Channel media uses the positive integer `DEEPAGENTS_TALON_MAX_MEDIA_BYTES` cap, with a shared default of 1 GiB; adapters validate outbound type, trusted-root containment, and size before upload.
